subject: Archaeology
title: Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon
description: A quick, practical guide to Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon.

hook.text: Nebuchadnezzar II made Babylon the most magnificent city on earth — and destroyed Jerusalem's temple to do it.

buildup.text: He rebuilt Babylon with massive walls, the Ishtar Gate, a towering ziggurat, and grand processional streets.

discovery.text: He conquered Jerusalem in 586 BCE and deported thousands of Jews to Babylon — the Babylonian Exile shaped Judaism.

twist.text: Babylon in the Bible is a symbol of evil. But for Babylonians, Nebuchadnezzar was a hero who built a golden age.

climax.text: Alexander the Great intended to make Babylon his capital. He died there in 323 BCE before he could rebuild it.

punchline.text: One king made it a wonder. Another tried to revive it.

quiz.question: What major religious event did Nebuchadnezzar cause?
options: He converted the Babylonian Empire to monotheism
He destroyed Jerusalem's temple and deported Jews — the Babylonian Exile
He ordered the writing of the first version of the Torah

details.summary: Nebuchadnezzar II rebuilt Babylon into the ancient world's most magnificent city around 600 BCE. He constructed the Ishtar Gate, massive defensive walls, and possibly the Hanging Gardens, making Babylon a wonder that awed visitors and inspired legends for millennia.
details.whyItMatters: Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon represents the peak of Mesopotamian urban achievement. Its archaeological remains confirm many biblical and classical descriptions, bridging ancient literature and physical evidence.
takeaways: Nebuchadnezzar II rebuilt Babylon around 600 BCE
He constructed the Ishtar Gate and massive defensive walls
Babylon's grandeur inspired legends that persisted for millennia

faq.question: How big was Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon?
faq.answer: Babylon covered roughly 10 square kilometers with massive double walls. Herodotus claimed the outer wall was wide enough for chariots to ride atop it. While his numbers are likely exaggerated, archaeological remains confirm an enormous, well-fortified urban center.

faq.question: Did Nebuchadnezzar really destroy Jerusalem?
faq.answer: Yes. Archaeological and biblical evidence confirm that Nebuchadnezzar conquered Jerusalem in 586 BCE, destroyed Solomon's Temple, and deported many inhabitants to Babylon. This event shaped Jewish history and theology profoundly.
